Below it a heading "PSALMVS CXXXVI." then a verse psalm in one stanza block, ending with the initials "I. L. G." right-aligned. Below a rule, a second heading "CANTICVM" with a subtitle in two lines, then a verse canticle, one stanza block. Full width throughout; no margin notes.

main_text.head: PSALMVS CXXXVI.
main_text.p: NOs vbi captiuam Deus in patria arua Sio- nem Abriperet, certe somnia vana rati, Tunc nostra implerunt ora exultantia cantus, Nostra dedit laetos lingua canora sonos. Grande opus his Deus edit, ait gens plurima, nobis Edit grande Deus quo recreamur opus. Eia reduc trifti captiuam e carcere gentem, Sicut in arentes grata fluenta locos. Ille canens repetat sublatis tecta manibus, Qui lacrymis sparsit semina chara suis. I. L. G.
main_text.head: CANTICVM Mariae Virginis Sanctissimae Domini nostri Iesu Christi matris.
main_text.p: TE, Pater alme, canit mea mes, te exultat in vno Spiritus, o mea spes, o mea sola Salus, Qui de sydereo sublimis culmine caeli Res ancillae humiles respicis ecce tuae. Hinc erit vt longum felix ego dicar in aeuum, Et populi aeterna laude per ora ferar. Ille etenim, cuius nunquam finita potestas, Qui Sanctum augusto Numine nomen habet,

page.notes: Scan is a verse page with occasional show-through from the reverse (faint mirrored text in the margins and between the stanzas) which is omitted. The first capitals are large decorative initials (N, T), joined to their words as "NOs" and "TE". Several stanza lines are italic; "Quì" and "Qui" appear with a superscript-style accent that is not reproduced. Doubtful: "Ille canens repetat sublatis tecta manibus" and "Qui lacrymis sparsit semina chara suis" are read from a slightly blurred line; "sublatis" and "manibus" may be off.
